source_metadata.exact_title: KDIGO 2026 Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) and Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) — Public Review Draft
source_metadata.source_type: clinical practice guideline public-review draft with data supplement

consistency_findings: Recommendation strength and certainty of evidence are kept distinct; a Level 1 recommendation can coexist with low-certainty evidence under the guideline framework.
Evidence-profile atoms are explicitly tagged as secondary evidence synthesis and are not represented as primary-study results.
The main document and data supplement are treated as one source packet with one publication identity and file-specific provenance hashes.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no guideline_recommendation, practice_point, or evidence_profile atom kind. Guideline statements and evidence-profile synthesis conclusions are represented as author_conclusion atoms with descriptive tags.

The current schema does not encode recommendation strength or GRADE certainty as dedicated typed fields; these remain in canonical text and tags rather than being invented as unsupported structured fields.
extraction_limitations: The bibliography was not atomized because reference entries are provenance infrastructure rather than independently generated evidence from the guideline.

The guideline reports evidence from underlying studies; those reports were not converted into primary-study atoms. Primary publications should be extracted separately when primary-study atoms are required.

Evidence-profile extraction captures the source-authored balance-of-benefits-and-harms conclusion and overall certainty for 131 profiles; it does not atomize every row-level effect estimate in all 140 evidence profiles.
All atoms remain needs_review because this is automated extraction from a public-review draft rather than human verification.
